claims.statement: The European Commission says the definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026 and importers above the 50-tonne threshold must become authorized declarants, declare embedded emissions and surrender purchased certificates.

The Commission published 2026 quarterly certificate prices of 75.36 EUR for Q1 and 75.28 EUR for Q2 and says purchases on the common platform begin from February 2027, making 2026 imports a measurable upcoming cash liability rather than an August 2026 certificate purchase.

The 50-tonne simplification is expected by the Commission to exempt about 182,000 importers while retaining over 99% of covered emissions, concentrating the opportunity in fewer, generally larger accounts.
Supplier-data reuse and liability forecasting may support SaaS margins, but regulation does not prove customers will buy from a new vendor.

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold removes most small importers, leaving accounts with longer security, procurement and liability reviews.
Customs brokers, ERP vendors and major consultancies are natural incumbents, and default emission values may reduce near-term supplier-data urgency.
Regulatory changes, circumvention rules and certificate timing can change product requirements.

economics.acquisition_route: Partner with customs brokers, freight forwarders, metal and fertilizer distributors, accountants and trade-finance banks; sell a fixed-fee liability diagnostic before an annual contract.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable supplier-installation records, CN mappings, evidence-quality scores, verified emission histories and resolution patterns can reduce repeated requests across importer customers while respecting confidentiality.
fingerprint.customer: Polish and CEE importers and indirect customs representatives handling more than 50 tonnes per year of covered cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilizer, electricity or hydrogen goods.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner with customs brokers, freight forwarders, metal and fertilizer distributors, accountants and trade-finance banks; sell a fixed-fee liability diagnostic before an annual contract.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Ingest customs lines, map CN codes, open a multilingual supplier evidence portal, validate units and periods, flag when defaults or verification are required, forecast certificate quantity and price exposure and preserve deductions for carbon price paid abroad.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer bears the mandatory certificate liability tied to emissions and would pay an annual platform fee plus supplier or customs-line volume pricing. Certificate purchase is concrete; a separate compliance-software budget is not established by regulation and must be validated.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Each in-scope import creates embedded-emissions data requirements and a future certificate liability; the importer must maintain authorized status, collect installation data or defaults, prove foreign carbon price where relevant, forecast certificate cash and complete the annual declaration and surrender.

founder_fit: Strong EU, finance, quantitative and data-workflow fit.
Can start with software and managed data validation rather than capital-intensive operations.
Broker distribution can reach importers without a public founder persona.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: CBAM supplier-data and certificate-liability cockpit
uncertainties: Number and import concentration of reachable above-threshold Polish and CEE firms by sector.
How much compliance work customs representatives already bundle and at what price.
Supplier willingness to share installation data and the legal ability to reuse it across importers.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Obtain permissioned 2026 customs extracts from 25 potential importers, calculate scope and certificate liability using both actual and allowed default data, and quantify missing evidence and forecast variance. Sell the diagnostic at a fixed fee, then require at least three annual contracts through one broker before building deeper registry integrations.
